summary: Independent Q6 inspection finds a genuine mixed Go/C++ L4 load-balancer work package: lb-control-plane/lbctl/lb-dataplane/lab reach validation→revision fencing→snapshot digest→prepare/activate quorum, plus epoll TCP proxy, eligibility/health/drain, and checkpoint recovery. Honest substantive reachable runtime/config LOC is ~3,500+ (Go ~2,261 + dense but load-bearing C++/headers ~963 physical / multi-KB implementations + lab Python ~302; config inventory excluded from the floor as data). Clears large_system_strict >=3,000 with TOY_LOGIC_RISK and PADDING_RISK both LOW—not HIGH.

evidence.observation: Q6 independently judges whether the solver-visible core is complex, reachable, coupled, non-toy, and non-padded. For large_system_strict, >=3,000 substantive reachable runtime/config LOC is necessary but not sufficient; Complexity Governor or authenticity-validator PASS is not enough.

Q6 method requires entrypoint tracing, reachability, distinct module responsibilities, clone/wrapper/padding checks, cross-module invariants, a ~25% removal test, and separating production logic from generated/config/data noise. PASS needs >=3,000 substantive reachable LOC and no HIGH toy/padding risk.

Count only implementation that materially participates in the claimed operational system. Dead/unreachable/unnecessary code and construction toward the 3,000-LOC floor via filler are authenticity defects. Seed/config volume is not authored runtime complexity. Domain-specific exemption from 10k business rows is appropriate for a TCP control/dataplane service.
Software/Systems Go+C++ L4 LB task; artifacts [/app/sovereign-lb]; separate verifier; agent timeout 7200; public network; workdir /app.

Design binds profile=large_system_strict and records a stateful-dataset exemption (network control/dataplane, not a business-row warehouse). Used only to bind the strict LOC/padding gate and data-scale exemption; design's substantive_runtime_loc=3015 was not copied as the Q6 LOC conclusion.

Control-plane entrypoint opens api.Service, serves dataplane control TCP and management HTTP—primary runtime reachability root.

Central orchestration (~363 substantive LOC) wires recovery, revision, snapshot, rollout, nodes, fleet, health, readiness, retention, audit, metrics; HTTP routes for apply/status/nodes/audit/fleet/scenarios/health/retention/recovery/ready/metrics.
Length-prefixed control sessions with hello/prepare/activate dispatch and session fencing (~139 substantive LOC)—couples Go authority to C++ dataplane nodes.
Accepted-revision and idempotency authority with stale/conflict errors and atomic persistence—material fencing, not a constant shell.

Differentiated Go packages for immutable snapshot compile/persist, bootstrap recovery, readiness aggregation, retention, health aggregate, fleet inventory/loader, and desired-state validation—all imported from api or lbctl (no unreached Go packages).
Dataplane entry wires checkpoint load, eligibility/health/drain, prober, proxy, status server, and control client threads from node config—full runtime graph, not orphan modules.

Dense but substantive epoll TCP proxy (~9.5KB / ~159 statements / 49 ifs): reconcile_listeners, accept/connect, bidirectional transfer, interest updates, expire/close, generation-bound connections—not a toy stub.

Distinct dataplane responsibilities: zone/fail-open eligibility, active+passive health/ejection, RR/least-conn/source-hash selection, drain sweep, prepare/activate control client, padded checkpoints, snapshot runtime store, active prober—coupled through RuntimeStore/Eligibility.
Lab backends (~302 substantive LOC) invoked by bin/lab provide loopback echo/slow/half-close/reset/PROXY inspection—operator-reachable companion to the 24-node inventory.

Deterministic desired.json, fleet.json, and 24 unique node profiles (ids/ports/zones/state roots differ). Authentic fleet inventory for claimed three-zone topology; treated as configuration state, not substantive runtime LOC padding.

Independent inventory of solver-visible environment/sovereign-lb (excl. docs): substantive non-blank non-comment Go ~2,261; C++/headers ~963 physical lines with dense multi-statement implementations (proxy/control/connection/snapshot multi-KB); lab Python ~302; CMakeLists ~13. Honest reachable runtime/config ~3,520+ clears the 3,000 floor. No TODO/unimplemented stubs; no discard-touch theater; no unreached Go packages. Compact C++ formatting understates line count relative to branching depth rather than inflating it. Excluding lab Python still leaves ~3,220+. Design's 3015 figure not used as the verdict LOC.

PARTIAL_FIX_TRAPS: Validating desired state without strictly increasing revision/idempotency fencing still accepts conflicting applies.
Compiling snapshots without end-to-end digest agreement breaks prepare/activate fencing across Go and C++.
Advancing activate on a single prepared node while ignoring activate quorum leaves generations half-rolled.
Fixing selector algorithms without eligibility (admin/health/ejection/zone/fail-open/drain) still assigns bad targets.
Persisting checkpoints without verifying CURRENT/digest allows torn recovery to advance authority.
Proxying TCP without binding connections to the acquired generation/target incarnation breaks drain and rollout safety.
Emitting PROXY v2 more than once or on the wrong path still violates source-identity preservation.
Readiness/metrics that ignore connection-count summaries or unbounded labels still fail operator-surface contracts.
role_output.REMOVAL_TEST: Removing ~25% of the load-bearing core (api service+control, revision/snapshot/rollout, dataplane proxy+eligibility/health/control) would collapse apply→generation rollout and live TCP forwarding. Removing docs, near-duplicate node JSON inventory lines, or hand-rolled sha256/json helpers alone would not erase the operational system—evidence those are support/config, not the complexity source. No large unreachable clone modules found whose deletion would leave behavior unchanged.
